title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-20
content:
2026-03-04 daily scratchpad - GPU ops / infra

Top of mind:
- Week of capacity check: 75% reserved GPUs used on west-1, expected bump Wed/Thu due to batch evals from model-team. Need to ensure no preemption on dedicated pools.
- Burst pool config review: still default 2x allowance, consider temporary 3x for Wed 09:00-18:00 window for nightly evals.
- Network: flaky ops reported on nid-04 (10.12.4.0/24) during rolling kernel upgrade last night. Packet drops ~0.2% for ~20m. Follow-up with infra-net.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Confirm with model-team owners (cc Marco) about eval schedule and if they can shift to Fri (low traffic). (est 15m)
- [ ] Update burst policy on prod dedicated pools for 2026-03-04 08:00 UTC -> 2026-03-05 08:00 UTC if no better option. (est 10m)
- [ ] Open INF ticket for nid-04 network flakiness; attach tcpdump from 2026-03-03 23:45 window. (INF-342 exists, updating) (est 20m)
- [ ] Run quick capacity simulation for west-1 for +15% spike using scripts/capacity_sim.py and share to #infra-monitoring. (est 30m)
- [ ] Add a note to run full KV cache warmup after kernel rollout next maintenance window. (est 5m)

Commands / quick refs:
- Check GPU utilization (west-1): ssh infra@jump && ./scripts/gpu-check --region west-1 --since 24h
- Burst config CLI: infractl pools update --name dedicated-prod-west --burst-multiplier 3 --until 2026-03-05T08:00:00Z
- Grab tcpdump from nid-04: scp ops@nid-04:/var/log/tcpdump/2026-03-03-23.pcap ./tmp/ && wireshark ./tmp/2026-03-03-23.pcap
- Capacity sim: python3 tools/capacity_sim.py --region west-1 --spike 0.15 --duration 6h --out out/west1-15pct.json

Notes from standup (2026-03-04):
- Priya: autoscaler jitter observed on 2x->1x transitions; suspect race with batch scheduler. She will instrument with histogram metrics.
- Marco: model-team pushing larger eval; asked for dedicated queue but OK to use burst if we can limit to 3x.
- SRE: rolling kernel upgrades approved but we need to tighten pre-checks (net latency, mem pressure).

Incidents / recent events:
- 2026-03-03 23:35 - rolling kernel upgrade started on west-1 hosts. nid-04 showed transient packet loss (~0.2%) for ~20m correlated with reboots. No model-serving impact detected but internal healthcheck spikes.
- Action: keep nid-04 out of autoscale for next 48h until we verify stability; tag host with "maintenance-observed".

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can burst multiplier be limited per-customer to avoid noisy-neighbor during spikes? (ask product for policy)
- Is there a way to pre-warm KV caches automatically after host reboots? (talk to serving-runtime team)
- Should we add a pre-rollout network probe step (iperf3 + small tcp probe) to kernel rollout checklist?

Quick plan for today:
- 09:00 - run capacity_sim and publish results in #infra-monitoring (me)
- 10:00 - sync with Marco on eval timings and propose Fri shift (10m)
- 11:00 - update burst policy if no blocker (me / infractl)
- 14:00 - follow-up on INF-342 with network team (Priya to join)
- 16:30 - triage outstanding alerts and ensure nid-04 healthchecks are green for 2h window

Notes to self (random):
- Remember to bump the bump-log retention to 14d for kernel-upgrade logs; current retention 7d bites when triaging late.
- If Marco insists on Wed, schedule quiet-window for other non-critical batch jobs 09:00-18:00 to reduce comp contention.

Attachments / links:
- JIRA: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-342 (update with tcpdump)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/128 (burst policy CLI change)
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/GPU+Capacity+Plan

End of scratchpad. Will move actionable items into INF board after noon once confirmed.
